Warm-up: say one word you already know for this topic.

Which word belongs to this topic?
Core Active Vocabulary (10 items):

room — a part of a building with walls. Example: My room is small.
floor — the surface you walk on. Example: The book is on the floor.
wall — the side of a room. Example: There is a picture on the wall.
clothes — the things you wear. Example: The clothes are on the bed.
books — things you read. Example: There are books on the desk.
toys — things children play with. Example: The toys are in the box.
mess — a place that is not tidy. Example: My room is a mess.
clean — not dirty. Example: The floor is clean now.
tidy — neat and in order. Example: Please keep your room tidy.
bin — a container for rubbish. Example: Put the paper in the bin.
Essential Chunks & Functional Collocations:

• What a mess!
• There is a ... on the floor.
• There are ... on the bed.
• Let's tidy up.
• Put it in the bin.

There is becomes /ðeəz/, there are becomes /ðeərə/.

Listen and repeat three times.
Which word carries the main stress?
Grammar focus: There is / There are.
Use there is with one thing and there are with many things: There is a book on the floor. There are clothes on the bed.
Controlled practice: choose the correct option.
Choose the correct sentence.
options: There is a book on the floor.
There are a book on the floor.
There is books on the floor.

elements.content: Reading: read the text and answer the questions.
My room is a mess. There are clothes on the floor and books on the desk. There is a bin near the door but it is full.
Listening: listen to the dialogue and answer the questions.
A: What a mess! B: I know. There are toys on the floor. A: And there is a cup on the shelf. B: I will tidy it now.
Speaking: Pair and group tasks: Describe a picture of a messy room; decide what to tidy first.

• What a mess!
• There is a ... on the floor.
• There are ... on the bed.
Writing: Write four to five sentences about "What a Mess" using the target grammar.
